analysis:
The changes in EngineV2Bridge.swift add state and an init parameter for deadline admission: observedDecodeStep (head 319), admissionFixes (321, set at 411), calibratedIsolatedPrefillTps (336), and a line at 508 that sets performanceMeasurements.keepsNewestObservationTime. The added file AdmissionRateEstimators.swift introduces DeadlineAdmissionFixes, an env-gated switch (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, default on), and the MeasuredDecodeStep estimator. I only had the new file's metadata and a truncated patch excerpt, not its full text.

From the supplied evidence these look like local scheduling and performance-estimation changes. I found no change to the A-001 plaintext path, the prefix cache or SSD tier (T-041), key custody, attestation or serving authorization (TB-011), or the coordinator wire contract.

The environment variable is read from the provider process environment, which the operator already controls (ADV-001). It only tunes admission estimators and does not widen a trust boundary. It also does not weaken the hard absolute-expiry checks noted in the bridge comments.

The one security-relevant question is availability. A wrong or manipulable rate estimate could cause over-admission or over-rejection. Inputs are measured from the provider's own requests, so a consumer could influence them only through request shape. Still unexamined: the consumers of observedDecodeStep and calibratedIsolatedPrefillTps (+Admission and the deadline engine paths), and the full body of MeasuredDecodeStep, including division-by-zero, NaN or overflow handling. None of that was supplied, so I am not filing a finding. Because the full new file was not visible, I am flagging a deeper review of the estimator math and its callers.
